Yet I can hardly believe this, for *Cauda* <note>the Dragon's Tail, or South Node</note> in a human sign usually yields slanders rather than truths; it is a hundred to one if she does not suffer in her reputation among the common people <note>this was too true</note>. Besides, the closeness of *Venus* to *Saturn* may well show trouble of mind; and since it is in the *Ninth House*, please inquire whether she has not been troubled about some tenets of religion <note>the trouble of mind was real, but it was about a stranger, which the Ninth House also signifies</note>.

Diagnostica.] *Venus*, Lady of the *Twelfth*, the *Ascendant*, and the *Eighth*, shows her always to be her own enemy regarding her health; and truly, I believe the origin of the disease was a surfeit caused either by eating moist fruits or else by catching a chill while traveling. *Venus* with *Saturn*, who is in square to the *Ascendant*, troubles her *breasts* with tough *phlegm* and *melancholy*. Besides, as there is a very strong reception between the *Moon* and *Venus* in fertile signs, I wonder whether or not she is pregnant, the *Moon* being in the *Fifth House*. *Mars* is the Lord of the Disease; being essentially in *Scorpio* and accidentally in the *Ascendant*, together with *Aries* on the *Sixth house*, shows the disease holds court in the *womb* and accidentally afflicts the *head* from there. Thus, heat of the womb must be the cause of the present illness; and *Mars* in a moist sign in the first house near the second may well denote heat and breakouts around her *face* and *throat*.

Prognostica.] Whether she will be curable or not, or how or when the disease will end, is our next point. Truly, I can see no danger of death, the *Moon* being strong in her *hayz* <note>a favorable astrological position; the original text says "Hain"</note> and applying by *trine* with a strong reception to the Lady of the *Ascendant*. Yet this is certain: *Mars* being strong in a fixed sign will maintain the disease stubbornly. Her hopes will be small when *Venus* reaches the body of *Saturn*—namely, on *August 2*—for she will be overwhelmed with *melancholy*. The time I expect for her cure (if proper steps are taken) may be when *Mars* leaves the sign he is in and reaches the position of the body of *Jupiter*; or at least, then it may turn into another, more favorable disease. The *Sun* being strong in the *Tenth house* shows she may be cured by medicine; and since he is exalted in the *Seventh* along with *caput* <note>Caput Draconis, the Dragon's Head or North Node</note> there, I believe you are as likely a man to achieve it as anyone.

Indicationes Curativæ.] It is acknowledged here that the *Sun*, being exceedingly strong in the *tenth house*, should naturally signify the curative medicine; and it is just as true that the evil of *Mars*—namely, heat of the womb and a salt humor in the blood—ought to be removed before you deal with the tough phlegm in the breast. But yet, seeing as the disease seems to involve an offensive heat rather than any other simple quality, you must be careful with hot medicines, lest you attempt to *extinguish fire with oil* <note>ignem oleo extinguere</note>. The medicines must be, first, cooling; second, strengthening the womb; third, repressing the vapors; and fourth, of the nature of the *Sun* and *Venus*.

Therapeutice.] To this end, I first recommend to you stinking *Arrach* <note>Stinking Goosefoot, Chenopodium vulvaria</note>, a sample of which I have sent enclosed here; you may find it on dung-hills,

It grows in bogs in uncultivated places and is in flower about this time. *I chose this figure specifically to judge, so that no one would have a just occasion to say of us astrologers that we act as physicians do in their common practice when they judge urine: they pump what they can out of the questioner <note>the patient or "querent"</note> and then judge by his words. Of this, I will recount one merry story for you, and so I will conclude the book.*

*A woman whose husband had bruised himself took his urine and trots off to the doctor. The doctor takes the urine and shakes it around. "How long has this person been ill?" he asks. "Sir," says the woman, "he has been ill these two days." "This is a man’s urine," says the doctor immediately; this he learned from the word "HE." Then, looking at the urine, he saw blood in it. "The man has had a bruise," he says. "Yes indeed," says the woman, "my husband fell down a flight of stairs backwards." Then the doctor, knowing well enough that whatever came first to danger must have been his back and shoulders, said the bruise was located there. The woman admired the doctor's skill and told him that if he could tell her one thing more, she would consider him the most capable physician in Europe. Well, what was that? How many stairs her husband fell down! This was a hard question indeed, able to puzzle a stronger brain than the Doctor had. He begins pumping, and having taken the urinal and given it a shake or two, he inquires about where she lived. Knowing the place well, and that the houses thereabouts were only low-built houses, he answered (after another view of the urine for appearance's sake) that probably he might have fallen down seven or eight stairs. "Ah," says the woman, "now I see you know nothing; my husband fell down thirty!" "Thirty!" says the Doctor, and snatching up the urinal, "Is all the urine here?" he asks. "No," says the woman, "I spilled some of it while putting it in." "Look there!" says the Doctor, "That is where all the other stairs were spilled."*

*Yet do not mistake me: I do not deny that those whose daily experience is to judge urines, and who usually judge a hundred in a day, may know something by them. If anything may be known by urine, I am sure it may be known by Art; put them both together: vis unita fortior <note>United strength is stronger</note>. Thus I take my leave of you; be diligent, and I am yours.*
